package_info.package_versions: 17.3.1 and below, 17.2.4 and below, 17.1.6 and below
package_info.why_malicious: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in affected GitLab versions allow attackers to exploit privilege escalation, server-side request forgery (SSRF), denial-of-service (DoS), and command injection. These flaws enable unauthorized access, data exfiltration, remote code execution, and compromise of critical infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (pipeline trigger via API or UI)
execution_context.file_location: GitLab backend (pipeline trigger logic, likely in app/services/ci/create_pipeline_service.rb or related controller)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker triggers a pipeline as another user due to improper authentication/authorization checks (CVE-2024-6678).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a pipeline is triggered via API or UI, the code fails to properly authenticate and authorize the user context, allowing an attacker to specify an arbitrary user and trigger a CI/CD pipeline as that user, resulting in privilege escalation and unauthorized code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing a non-privileged user to trigger actions as another user without their consent enables privilege escalation and unauthorized access to sensitive operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only authenticated users should be able to trigger pipelines on their own behalf, and user context should be strictly enforced; this flaw allows impersonation by unprivileged users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Impersonation may be used by administrators for debugging or support purposes, but should never be accessible to regular or unprivileged users.
key_indicators: Pipeline trigger endpoint lacks strict user validation and authorization checks
Ability to specify or override user context in pipeline trigger requests
Pipeline logs showing triggers by users who did not initiate the action

execution_context.trigger: runtime (dependency proxy request via Maven endpoint)
execution_context.file_location: Maven Dependency Proxy URL handler (GitLab EE backend, likely in ee/lib/ee/api/dependency_proxy.rb or related controller)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker crafts a custom Maven Dependency Proxy URL to perform SSRF (CVE-2024-8635).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when processing a user-supplied Maven Dependency Proxy URL, the code fails to validate or sanitize the URL, allowing the attacker to supply arbitrary URLs that the server fetches, resulting in server-side request forgery and potential access to internal resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Permitting user-controlled URLs to be fetched by the server can be abused to access internal-only resources, bypassing network boundaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Dependency proxy should only fetch legitimate, external Maven artifacts from trusted sources, not arbitrary or internal URLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching dependencies from public Maven repositories is legitimate, but only when URLs are validated and restricted to known domains.
key_indicators: Lack of URL sanitization or allowlist enforcement in dependency proxy handler
Ability to specify internal IP addresses or hostnames in dependency proxy requests
Dependency proxy logs showing requests to non-standard or internal network locations

execution_context.trigger: runtime (API request with large glm_source parameter)
execution_context.file_location: API endpoint handling glm_source parameter (likely in app/controllers/api/ or related parameter parsing logic)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a large glm_source parameter to cause DoS (CVE-2024-8124).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when handling API requests containing the glm_source parameter, the code does not enforce a maximum size limit, allowing an attacker to send an excessively large value that consumes server memory and processing resources, resulting in denial-of-service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unbounded input parameters can be exploited to exhaust server resources, leading to service crashes or degraded availability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: API parameters should be strictly size-limited and validated to prevent resource exhaustion attacks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Large parameters may be used for legitimate data transfer, but should always be subject to reasonable size constraints.
key_indicators: No input size validation or limit on glm_source parameter
API logs showing requests with abnormally large glm_source values
Resource exhaustion or high memory usage correlated with large parameter input

execution_context.trigger: runtime (Cube server command execution via integration logic)
execution_context.file_location: Cube server integration logic (GitLab EE backend, likely in ee/app/services/cube_server_service.rb or related integration code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker injects commands into Cube server due to incomplete input filtering (CVE-2024-8640).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when processing user-supplied input for Cube server integration, the code passes input directly to command execution interfaces without sufficient sanitization, enabling command injection and arbitrary command execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Passing unsanitized user input to command execution interfaces is a classic injection vector, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should be strictly validated and escaped before being used in any command execution context to prevent injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate commands may be constructed from user input, but only after thorough validation and sanitization to prevent injection.
key_indicators: Lack of input sanitization or escaping in Cube server integration logic
Direct concatenation or interpolation of user input into command strings
Cube server logs showing unexpected or anomalous command patterns

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies a vulnerable GitLab instance and crafts malicious requests targeting one or more of the disclosed vulnerabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation, internal resource access, denial-of-service, or remote command execution depending on the vulnerability exploited.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-6678 is exploited, attacker triggers pipelines as other users by bypassing authentication, potentially running arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation and potential unauthorized code execution within CI/CD pipelines.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-8635 is exploited, attacker uses SSRF via the Maven Dependency Proxy to access internal services or sensitive metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Internal data exposure, access to internal APIs, or further lateral movement within the network.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-8124 is exploited, attacker sends a large glm_source parameter in API requests to exhaust server resources and cause denial-of-service.
attack_chain.leads_to: Service unavailability or degraded performance due to resource exhaustion.

attack_chain.action: If CVE-2024-8640 is exploited, attacker injects commands into Cube server integration, achieving arbitrary command execution on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and potential full compromise of the GitLab server.

behavioral_signatures: CI/CD pipeline triggered by users who did not initiate the action or by unauthorized accounts
Dependency proxy requests to internal or non-standard URLs, especially those resolving to private IP ranges
API requests containing abnormally large glm_source parameter values exceeding expected limits
User-supplied input passed directly to command execution interfaces in Cube server integration
file_indicators: Pipeline logs showing user impersonation or mismatched user IDs in trigger events
Dependency proxy logs with requests to internal IP addresses or hostnames (e.g., 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8, localhost)
API logs with glm_source parameter values significantly larger than typical usage
Cube server logs containing unexpected command arguments or anomalous command patterns
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitLab server to internal network addresses or metadata endpoints
High volume of API requests with large payloads targeting glm_source parameter
Unexpected outbound connections or command-and-control traffic following command injection attempts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD pipeline trigger logs for evidence of user impersonation or unauthorized triggers. Inspect dependency proxy logs for requests to internal or non-standard URLs, and set alerts for any requests resolving to private IP ranges. Implement input size validation and alerting for API requests with excessively large glm_source parameters. Audit Cube server integration logs for unsanitized user input and anomalous command execution patterns. Deploy WAF rules to block suspicious payloads, enforce strict input validation on all user-supplied data, and regularly review logs for indicators of exploitation.
